tool_input.command: for f in routes/web.ts routes/auth.ts routes/admin.ts src/app.ts src/main.ts app/Http/Controllers/AdminPostController.ts; do echo "===== $f ====="; cat "$f"; done

result:
Both gates pass: `bun run typecheck` clean, `bun test` 3 pass / 0 fail.

The endpoint's code was complete but orphaned: `routes/admin.ts` exported `registerAdminRoutes`, and nothing ever called it — `src/app.ts` mounts only `registerWebRoutes`, so `/admin/posts` was never added to the router and fell through to the 404 handler for guests and signed-in users alike. I mounted it in `routes/web.ts:21` with `registerAdminRoutes(router)`, placed right after `registerAuthRoutes(router)` and before the `/posts` group, passing the same `baseRouter`-derived router that carries the `auth`/`guest` middleware aliases — which is exactly what `routes/admin.ts` expects via its `Router<'auth'>` signature, so the route lands behind the same `requireAuthenticated({ redirectTo: '/login' })` alias as `/dashboard` and `/profile`. I then re-ran `bun run codegen`, which picked the new route up into `.guren/routes.gen.ts` (`admin.posts.index` → `GET /admin/posts`, plus the `routes.admin.posts.index()` helper), `types/generated/routes.d.ts` (`'/admin/posts'` in `RoutePath`), and the API client. I added `tests/AdminPostController.test.ts` asserting a guest is redirected to `/login` rather than 404'd — the fixture-free half of the behaviour — and separately verified the authenticated path against the seeded dev database with a throwaway test (since removed): it returns `200` with `{"data":[{"id":2,...,"author":{"id":1,"name":"..."}},{"id":1,...}]}`, newest first. No controller, resource, or model code changed.
